cards.stem: How is weight described in terms of earth attraction?
options: the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth
a mechanical force requiring contact with air
a lift force created by wing shape
a drag force from air friction
cards.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.
cards.hint: Recall the opening definition distinguishing weight from aerodynamic forces.

cards.stem: What type of force is gravity described as regarding contact?
cards.quote: The gravitational force is a field force; the source of the force does not have to be in physical contact with the object to generate a force.
cards.hint: Think about whether the source must touch the object to act.

cards.stem: What is the value of gravitational acceleration at earth surface in metric units?
cards.quote: On the surface of the earth, its value is 9.8 meters per square second or 32.2 feet per square second.
cards.hint: Focus on the metric value given for the surface.

cards.stem: What is expected to happen to weight when distance from earth center grows?
cards.quote: we would expect that the weight of an object would decrease with altitude.
cards.hint: Consider how gravity changes with height.
